title: What I Wish I Said: Confessions of a Columnist
author: Jackie Hill Perry
target_audience: Fans of Jackie Hill Perry’s writing and podcasting
Readers interested in candid life reflections
Individuals navigating faith, culture, and personal growth
People seeking Christian perspectives on everyday dilemmas
Women looking for thoughtful truths about work, relationships, and spirituality
primary_purpose: To share personal confessions, behind-the-scenes thoughts, and deeper reflections related to previously published columns—offering readers the context, faith perspective, and hard truths that often go unspoken.

structure_format.organization: Collection of essays or short chapters, each expanding beyond published columns to include the ‘things left unsaid’
features: Brief columns followed by longer reflective essays

key_concepts_lessons: True connection requires vulnerability and honesty.
The advice or answers we give publicly are often just the tip of deeper, more complicated realities.
God’s truth and grace shape our confessions and growth.
There is power and healing in owning what we haven’t said or couldn’t say.
Faith applies to the mundane, not just the extraordinary.
notable_features: Emphasis on what is left unsaid in public platforms
Candid insight into the life of a columnist and public Christian figure
Addresses both lighthearted and serious life topics
cultural_historical_context: Written in the 2020s, the book reflects contemporary conversations about authenticity, vulnerability, and the intersection of personal faith with cultural and public life. Jackie Hill Perry draws from her experience as a poet, author, and podcast host, engaging readers attuned to confessional storytelling.
reception_impact: Well-received by Christian readers and Perry’s followers
Praised for its vulnerability and honesty
Offers relatable truths for a variety of ages, especially women
Some critics note it is most resonant for readers with existing faith backgrounds
